# AMD Instinct Data Center Design Guide

> An overview of AMD Instinct data center architecture for high-density AI and HPC deployments. Covers the challenges of dense, high-powered racks, raised floor versus concrete slab construction, physical layout and cooling strategies (hot/cold aisle isolation, RDHx, DLC, and hybrid approaches), ORV3 open-standard racks, backend network design (fat tree and rail-optimized topologies), centralized control planes, centralized and federated storage, and power feed and resiliency design.

## Topics

- [Challenges](https://instinct.docs.amd.com/projects/dc-design/latest/index.html#challenges): Compounding challenges of dense, high-powered racks—power delivery, cooling, physical space and floor loading, cable management, energy efficiency and PUE, safety and risk, operational complexity, and non-linear CapEx/OpEx cost implications.
- [Raised floor versus concrete slab](https://instinct.docs.amd.com/projects/dc-design/latest/index.html#raised-floor-versus-concrete-slab): Trade-offs between raised floor and concrete slab architectures for cooling, power distribution, liquid cooling, structural load, scalability, and cost, with concrete slab generally preferred for ultra-high-density AI deployments.
- [Physical layout](https://instinct.docs.amd.com/projects/dc-design/latest/index.html#physical-layout): Patterns of organization (rows of racks, RDHx rows, hot/cold aisle islands, modular datacenters) and cooling strategies including hot/cold aisle isolation, rear door heat exchangers, hybrid DLC plus air or RDHx, and the move to ORV3 open-standard racks.
- [Network Design](https://instinct.docs.amd.com/projects/dc-design/latest/index.html#network-design): Cluster network types (management/out-of-band, public access, storage, and backend accelerator fabric) and backend fabric topologies, comparing fat tree and rail-optimized designs for AI and HPC workloads.
- [Centralized Control Plane](https://instinct.docs.amd.com/projects/dc-design/latest/index.html#centralized-control-plane): Unified orchestration, infrastructure abstraction, telemetry and monitoring, control APIs, and security for managing compute, networking, power, and cooling at scale, with integration into AI workloads.
- [Storage](https://instinct.docs.amd.com/projects/dc-design/latest/index.html#storage): Centralized modular storage and federated pod-level storage architectures, covering parallel and object file systems, tiered storage, scalability strategies, and integration with AI and HPC training workflows.
- [Power considerations](https://instinct.docs.amd.com/projects/dc-design/latest/index.html#power-considerations): High-voltage and modular power feed design, redundancy and scalability, components of a high-power feed system, integration with cooling, and safety considerations for extreme rack densities.
- [Power resiliency](https://instinct.docs.amd.com/projects/dc-design/latest/index.html#power-resiliency): Redundant power architecture, on-site energy storage, backup generation, microgrids, dynamic load management, and fault detection for continuous availability of mission-critical AI/HPC workloads.
